predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1, 'Feature Distillation and Language Alignment for 3D Zones'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The method defines zones as 'uniform cubic zones (each spanning several cubic meters)' aggregating instance features within each zone. However, for training the zone encoder, the paper states: 'it uses a zone encoder to aggregate 3D instances that belong to the same 2D view... Although the aggregated instances do not strictly come from the same cube zone, this approach ensures the quality of the distilled ground-truth features.' This is an explicit admission that the training supervision signal (instances from the same 2D view) does not match the actual zone definition used at inference (cubic spatial partitions), creating a train/inference mismatch that undermines the claimed zone-level representation learning.

The prose introduces the 3D instance feature as ℰ_i ('Given a 3D instance feature ℰ_i and its corresponding annotated language description feature T_i...'), but Equations 5, 6, and 7 all use the symbol 𝒪_i (e.g., 'CosSim(𝒪_i, T_j)', 'CosSim(𝒪_i, 𝒪_j^{gt})') instead of ℰ_i for what appears to be the same instance representation. This inconsistent notation makes the formal definitions ambiguous and internally inconsistent.
